stem.text: The function f is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of f are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 1 < c < 5 \), for which \( f(c) = -1 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: Yes. Since f is differentiable, it is continuous on \( [2, 3] \), and \( f(2) = -9 < -1 < f(3) = 3 \), so the Intermediate Value Theorem gives at least one such c.

worked_solution.text: Because f is differentiable, f is continuous, in particular on \( [2, 3] \).
From the table, \( f(2) = -9 < -1 < f(3) = 3 \), so -1 lies between the values of f at the ends of \( [2, 3] \).
By the Intermediate Value Theorem there is at least one c with \( 2 < c < 3 \) and \( f(c) = -1 \), and that c also satisfies \( 1 < c < 5 \). So yes, such a c must exist.
